name: usgs-earthquakes
title: Earthquakes in the USGS catalog, 2024 and 2025
summary: Count, sort and measure earthquakes in the US Geological Survey's catalog: magnitude and depth classes, event types, local clocks, distances across the 180-degree meridian, aftershocks, b-values and seismic moment.
description: Each task hands the AI one extract of the earthquake catalog, exactly as the US Geological Survey's public web service returned it in November 2026. The question states every measure it needs, such as class bounds, a point and a radius, a time window or a formula. The AI gives exact figures: counts, medians, distances, gaps, b-values and seismic moments. Every field of the answer is checked, and a task passes only when all of them are right.

families.name: Magnitude classes
families.what: Events counted into stated magnitude classes, with whole magnitudes written without a decimal point read right.

families.name: Magnitude types
families.what: Magnitude types kept apart by network and by size, and where moment magnitudes take over.

families.name: Depth classes
families.what: Events by depth class, with negative depths and the default depths handled as the question says.

families.name: Event types and review status
families.what: Earthquakes told apart from explosions and other events, and automatic records from reviewed ones.

families.name: Time grouping
families.what: Events grouped by UTC date and by a stated local clock, and how long after the event a record was last updated.

families.name: Extremes and gaps
families.what: The largest events, the time between large earthquakes, and days with and without events.

families.name: Distance
families.what: Great-circle distances, boxes and radii worked out exactly, across the 180-degree meridian too.

families.name: Sequences
families.what: Foreshocks and aftershocks of a large earthquake, in windows that start at its exact origin time.

families.name: Magnitude and moment
families.what: Gutenberg-Richter b-values, and seismic moment from the formula the question gives.

families.name: Data checks
families.what: Empty cells, identifiers checked against networks and sources, and possible double entries, with no false alarms.
